chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq al-Ahmar, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Abu al-Abbas, from Ja'far ibn Ismail, from Idris, from Abu al-Saib, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Talib performed the Aqeeqa for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the seventh day, and invited the family of Abu Talib. They said, 'What is this?' He said, 'The Aqeeqa of Ahmad.' They said, 'For what reason did you name him Ahmad?' He said, 'I named him Ahmad because of the praises of the inhabitants of the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.أَحْمَدَ: Ahmad (a name of the Prophet, meaning 'most praiseworthy')
key_terms.عَقَّ: Performed Aqeeqa (ritual sacrifice for a newborn)
key_terms.عَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa (the sacrifice offered on the occasion of a child's birth)
key_terms.مَحْمَدَةِ: Praises (plural of hamd, referring to divine or universal praise)

ai.seo_question: Why did Abu Talib name the Prophet Muhammad 'Ahmad' according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the pre-prophetic familial devotion of Abu Talib, who performed the Aqeeqa for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on the seventh day, establishing a precedent for this Sunnah. His explanation for naming him 'Ahmad'—referencing the praise of the inhabitants of the heavens and earth—underscores the divine nature of the Prophet's title, linking it to the universal acknowledgment of his status. This context reinforces the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's lineage and the early recognition of his unique spiritual identity within the household of Hashim.
